text: It is significant that coincident with the moves that are being made in the direction of closer cooperation between Hongkong and Canton certain proposals have been mooted for a modification of the edict barring from admission to Government and Government aided schools students who were absent from study on certain dates.

label: text
text: The period of this suspension, or expulsion as it was then generally regarded, was not mentioned when the attitude of Sir R. E. Stubbs was outlined by the Chairman of the Education board and it is understood that the penalty paid during the period that has elapsed since their having been de-arred from entrance has been advanced to the Government as sufficient for the students to have expiated their offence. The end of the school year has been suggested as the date when such stringent measures might no longer apply.

label: text
text: The Government attitude is expected to be announced shortly.

label: text
text: It may be recalled that at the Education meeting at which Sir R. E. Stubbs' attitude was endorsed, nearly all the members who spoke were in accord with that attitude but a few thought it was too severe. Father Valtorta thought that temporary suspension and postponement of examinations would meet the case. Mr. J. M. Alves suggested the formation of a "humiliation" class of strikers in each school would be sufficient punishment and Dr. Wan spoke at length or "the need for taking a more liberal and considerate view."

label: text
text: Dr. Pearce thought that the balance had been struck between justice and generous consideration. Now, if ever, was the time for emphasising the importance of discipline. The matter should be left to the heads of schools. No one else could do anything in the matter.

label: text
text: The Chairman's final remark was that he thought that the matter could be safely left with the headmasters who, he was sure, would be sympathetic in their consideration.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” also understands that the Government has under consideration the proposed raising of fees which was not the outcome of the strike but revision which was considered necessary in any event. Representations have been made that the present is hardly opportune for an extra financial burden to be imposed on parents and it is likely that the Government may postpone or mitigate the increases.

text: The great reason for it existing to-day than for several years, was the bountiful cotton crops of the world, and the world was assured of the most adequate supply.

label: text
text: An optimistic view of the future of the cotton industry was taken by Mr. Richard Brooks, in his presidential address at the annual meeting of the Manchester Cotton Association.

label: text
text:
Britain had 57,000,000 of the world's spindleage of 160,000,000. America's spindleage was 38,000,000 largely engaged in supplying domestic requirements, so it would be strange if we failed to receive our due share of any improvement in world buying.
The organised curtailment of the output had undoubtedly saved the industry from a serious financial crisis. Even now, despite the most optimistic outlook, curtailment was still essential to avert excessive over-production and curious prices.
The question of the "futures" market for Manchester was seriously engaging attention.

text: Professor MacNeill, referring to the statement issued by the Boundary Commission on the 23rd, said it was calculated to cause grave misconception.

label: text
text: Professor MacNeill's resignation was announced in the Day by President Cosgrave.

label: text

label: text
text: A message on London, November 22 said Professor John MacNeill's resignation as a member of the Irish Boundary Commission, which the Executive Council has accepted was announced by President Cosgrave, in a speech at Emyvale Moughan, as being "because he had lost faith in the other members of the Commission." President Cosgrave declared that he likewise had lost faith and was forced to the conclusion that the other members were swayed in the discharge of their judicial duty by threats and political influences brought to bear upon them.

text: A three-year old child, daughter of Mr. V. A. Rosario, residing at Kowloon, accidentally fell from the first floor veranda of the house into the street yesterday afternoon.

label: text
text: The girl sustained a fracture of the legs and other injuries to the body. The injuries being found to be serious, the child was removed to the Government Civil Hospital from the Kwong Wah Hospital where she was first taken for treatment immediately after the accident.

text: Serious allegations were made at a meeting of the Bradford Chamber of Commerce of heavy delay and miscarriage of mails from Britain to the Far East via Siberia.

label: text
text: Delegates asserted that many mails are missing and letters are tampered with apparently when passing through Soviet territory. The matter was referred to the Postmaster-General.

label: text
text: A semi-official message says: "In view of the refusal of the Chinese Government to sign an agreement regarding the through passenger communication between the Soviet railways and the Soviet and Japanese Chinese railway, the conference concerning the matter has been temporarily suspended on the suggestion of the Soviet delegates. The Russian and Japanese commission on goods traffic will begin work in a few days' time."

text: A further deposit of gilt-edged securities valued at £250,000 is being made with the Crown Agents for the Colonies in London by the Head Office of the Mercantile Bank of India, Ltd., as security for additional note issue by their Hongkong branch. It is proposed to put this money at the disposal of the Government in connection with the trade loan.

label: text
text: Heavy penalties were imposed by Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning on a number of illicit woodcutters, the defendants being all women of the coolie class.

label: text
text: A large gang were engaged in the wholesale destruction of a plantation at Shaukijwan West yesterday afternoon. Guards from the Forestry Department, assisted by officers from Divisional Inspector Blackman's Station, pounced on the culprits and arrested some, whilst others made their escape. In a subsequent raid on huts in the vicinity, large quantities of freshly cut wood were seized, the total making up a full lorry load.

label: text
text: Five of the defendants were fined $50 each, or in the alternative four weeks' hard labour whilst others were fined $40 and $20, or imprisonment in default.
